messages:
Maya: Hey team — incoming escalation from a trial customer (Zeta Inc) reporting a ~2000-credit drop overnight. They only run a scheduled embeddings job once an hour. Can someone help triage?

Anya: pinging SRE. Do we have the customer_id and a sample request id?

Maya: cust_zeta / internal request id `req_8a3f` from their scheduled job. They say the job kept retrying for ~45m. Not seeing corresponding errors in their app logs.

Maya: pasted the job log snippet:```
[2026-03-15T03:12:01Z] job start: embedding-batch id=job_449
[2026-03-15T03:12:15Z] attempt=1 sent batch size=128 tokens=...
[2026-03-15T03:12:16Z] success latency=110ms credits=12
[2026-03-15T03:13:20Z] attempt=2 sent batch size=128 reason=lease-expired code=LEASE_TTL_EXPIRED
[2026-03-15T03:13:21Z] requeued id=job_449 worker=background-ingest-3
[2026-03-15T03:13:22Z] attempt=1 sent batch size=128 credits=12
... repeated many times ...
```

Maya: you can see credits debited on each successful attempt. Looks like the worker re-enqueued and reprocessed the same batch.

Anya: Hmm. Could be a stale lease on the queue + no idempotency key on the background worker. If the lease TTL expired while the worker was processing, another worker re-acquired and re-sent to embeddings endpoint. We should check the message_id/dedup keys and whether the worker sets x-idempotency-key.

ingest-bot: event: message_ack_timeout job_449 lease_ttl=60s acquired_by=background-ingest-3 requeued_by=queue-master-2

Liam: I see the background-ingest service was recently rolled with the new `backoff_ms` change that reduced lease refresh frequency. That combined with occasional GC pause could cause `LEASE_TTL_EXPIRED` to trigger while the worker still had the batch in-memory. The embeddings endpoint will charge per successful call — we effectively double-billed when the second worker completed the same batch.

Liam: quick repro steps: 1) run ingest worker with lease_ttl=60s and a long-processing batch (simulate 90s work) 2) kill -STOP the worker for >60s 3) queue-master reassigns and new worker completes -> observe two successful embed calls and two credit debits.

Anya: Thanks. For immediate mitigation: 1) increase lease_ttl to 5m for ingest queue 2) make worker renew lease more frequently (heartbeat at 1/3 TTL) 3) add idempotency header to embeddings client using the batch checksum or job_id+batch_index so duplicate completions are ignored by billing.

Jared: For the customer side: we should refund the consumed credits for the duplicated batches. Maya, can you capture exact timestamps and the credit IDs so billing can reconcile? We'll do a promo top-up for the trial + a short note apologizing.

Maya: Captured. I exported their consumption rows: `consumption_ids: [cons_991, cons_992, cons_993, cons_994]` (these are the repeated attempts). Sending to billing now.

Jared: Confirmed — scheduled refund of 2400 credits (will reflect in 24h). Also flagging account so auto-regen promo doesn't run until we've patched.

Liam: I'll ship a hotfix to background-ingest to set `X-Idempotency-Key: <job_id>:<batch_index>` and bump the lease TTL to 5m. Will also add a server-side guard in embeddings service: ignore duplicate idempotency keys that arrived within 10m and do not double-count consumption if the signature matches.

Anya: I'll monitor for requeues over the next 72h and add an alert if requeue rate > 0.5% of ingest throughput.

Maya: Thanks all. Customer notified and refunded. Follow-up tasks: liam: PR + deploy hotfix (ETA 3h), anya: alerts + temp TTL bump (done), jared: refund issued (done). I'll close the ticket after 24h of no requeues. :white_check_mark:

Liam: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/background-ingest/pull/781 (hotfix + idempotency). ETA 2.5h including smoke tests.

Anya: added monitoring dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/ingest/requeue-rate - watchlist set to support oncall.

Maya: Closing loop — Zeta Inc confirmed credits posted back and is happy with the explanation. Leaving thread open for 24h in case of regressions.
